description:
You are a compliance officer auditing user accounts for potential security vulnerabilities. Please perform the following tasks:

1. List all user accounts with empty passwords on the system. To do this, check the /etc/shadow file. Only include users where the second field (password hash) is empty (i.e., the colon-separated field is blank).
2. For each user found in step 1, append their username to the log file /home/user/audit_empty_pw.log. Each username should appear on a new line; the log file should not include any extra characters or descriptions (just the usernames).
3. If no users with empty passwords are found, create the log file /home/user/audit_empty_pw.log containing exactly the single line: NONE

Output log file requirements:
- If ANY user(s) have empty passwords, the file should include ONLY their usernames, one per line. No extra spaces or blank lines.
- If NONE, the file should contain ONLY the line: NONE (in uppercase, with no trailing spaces).
truth:
Prior to the task, the /etc/shadow file contains at least one user account with an empty password hash field (e.g., a "testuser" entry of the form: testuser::19434:0:99999:7:::).

After the task is completed:
- If "testuser" was the only account with an empty password, /home/user/audit_empty_pw.log will exist and contain:
testuser

If instead there were no users with empty password hashes, /home/user/audit_empty_pw.log would contain:
NONE

The file /home/user/audit_empty_pw.log should NOT contain any other text, spaces, or blank lines.
